title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 11-13): Grothendieck is building a combinatorial calculus on a finite ordered set L, apparently a 'combinatorial oriented segment' (I, ω0, ω1), as the next page explains. Inside an ambient structure M (strata or cells ordered by a relation Z ≪ X), he considers 'M̂-presheaves' 𝔏: families of elements a (or I_a) and intervals I_{a,b}. Previous page (p. 11): 𝔏** is the reduction of 𝔏. It is obtained not by deleting the redundant elements but by composing the intervals adjacent to them. So (𝔏**)_0 = 𝔏_0 minus 𝔏_red, and (𝔏**)_1 consists of composites of maximal convex chains X_1 < x_1 < X_2 < … < X_n with x_i ◁ X_i, X_{i+1}. These chains correspond one-to-one with the convex components of 𝔏. The 'shadow' is Omb°_M(𝔏) = ∪_{X∈𝔏} Ouv°_M(X) = {Z ∈ M | ∃X ∈ 𝔏, Z ≪ X}, a downward-closed open set generated by 𝔏.

This page states the key theorem. Let 𝔏 be a non-empty M̂-presheaf. Then cos-Ψ°_M(𝔏) = cos-Ψ°(Omb°_M(𝔏)) = Omb°_M(𝔏*), where 𝔏* is the complementary presheaf. In words, the operation cos-Ψ° depends only on the shadow, and it sends the shadow of 𝔏 to the shadow of its complement. The operator is undefined on this page; it is perhaps a 'co-' or complement version of an operator Ψ°.

A long hypothesis block is struck through with diagonal lines. It set a = or δ𝔏 (origin of the boundary) and b = ex δ𝔏 (extremity). It required L_{<a} ∈ 𝔏 or a minimal, and L_{>b} ∈ 𝔏 or b maximal. It noted these follow from the hypothesis H_𝔏: either L has a least element or L_{<a} ≠ ∅ for all a, and either L has a greatest element or L_{>a} ≠ ∅ for all a. The deletion suggests the theorem was then meant to hold for any non-empty 𝔏.

Corollary 1, under H_𝔏 'pour simplifier': s-Ψ°_M(𝔏) = s-Ψ°_M(Omb°_M(𝔏)) = Omb°_M(𝔏**). This is the 'saturated' or 'simplified' version, giving the shadow of the reduced presheaf; formally it is the theorem applied twice, with s-Ψ playing the role of the composite. Corollary 2 begins with T ∈ Drap(L), a flag (chain) of L, and 'fragments' of L, and breaks off. The next page restarts with an 'autre présentation' from the case of combinatorial segments. The purpose seems to be a combinatorial duality or complement theory for the open sets of a stratified object (a poset of strata) indexed by subdivisions of a segment. This fits Grothendieck's 1986 'dévissage' / tame-topology programme.
errors: Statements cannot be verified: the operators cos-Ψ°, s-Ψ°, the complement 𝔏* and the relation ≪ are defined on earlier pages not provided.

The hypotheses were struck out but H_𝔏 is reinvoked in Corollary 1. It is unclear whether the theorem is meant without hypotheses or with H_𝔏 tacit; Grothendieck himself restarts the exposition on the next page ('Autre présentation'), suggesting dissatisfaction.

ideas.what: Shadow (Omb°) of a presheaf of elements and intervals as the union of open stars Ouv°(X) in a poset M
ideas.modern_name: down-set / open subset generated in the Alexandrov topology of a poset of strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Alexandrov topology); context of stratified spaces
ideas.where_published: related ideas sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (dévissage of stratified structures)

ideas.what: Theorem: a complement-type operator cos-Ψ° commutes with taking the shadow and sends the shadow of 𝔏 to the shadow of its complementary presheaf 𝔏*
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial complement / Alexander-type duality for interval-presheaves on a finite chain

ideas.what: Reduction 𝔏** by composing intervals adjacent to redundant elements (convex components)
ideas.modern_name: reduction of a subdivision / coarsening of an interval decomposition

ideas.what: Flags T ∈ Drap(L) and 'fragments' of L
ideas.modern_name: chains in a poset / order complex

missed.claim: Corollary 2 on flags T ∈ Drap(L) and fragments is begun and abandoned. The whole 1986 combinatorial theory of 'pseudo-segments', complementary presheaves and shadows in a stratified poset M appears never to have been written up or pursued.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a fragment of Grothendieck's late programme on combinatorial models of stratified (tame) spaces. Its interest lies mainly in reconstructing that programme; standalone novelty is unclear without the definitions from earlier pages.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean-looking duality statement in an unpublished 1986 combinatorial theory of stratified posets. However, the definitions are elsewhere, the content seems elementary order theory, and the page is mostly crossed out and restarted.
transcription_corrections: The presheaf is written as script 𝔏 (as on p. 11), not Φ.

The struck hypotheses read 'soit a = or δ𝔏, b = ex δ𝔏' (origine/extrémité of the boundary), with insertions 'si L_{<a} ∈ 𝔏 et' and 'si L_{>b} ∈ 𝔏 et' replacing 'si a est minimal' / 'si b est maximal'.
In Corollary 1, '[?]' is 'Hyp': 'Sous la condition Hyp, pour simplifier'.
The middle term of the theorem reads cos-Ψ°_M(Omb°_M(𝔏)), with M subscripts.
Archive page number '15' at bottom left; manuscript page number '12' at top.
